topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Larger SIW arrays exhibit increased phase shifts due to antenna element interactions, impacting beam steering accuracy and control system efficiency. This translates to reduced link capacity and increased latency.  This trade-off necessitates careful design choices to optimize gain while minimizing interference for optimal communication performance.
reference_context: SIW arrays suffer from increased path length leading to signal attenuation (loss). Substrate losses further amplify this effect, impacting radiation efficiency.  Larger SIW arrays exhibit higher phase shifts due to element interactions, affecting beam steering accuracy and control system efficiency. This translates to reduced link capacity and increased latency. The trade-off between array size for gain and mitigating the impact of phase shifts on network performance is crucial.
